messages:
maya: FYI - customers in eu-west are seeing frequent model fallback to v1-quant during peak windows. spikes line up with quota hits for a couple of Premium accounts. can we get better trace info in the Console?
jon: Can you paste an example request with headers and the trace you saw?
maya: yep, here's the routing headers from the request and the compact decision trace we captured: 
maya: `X-Redwood-Routing: tier=premium; region=eu-west; prefer_variant=v1a`
maya: ````
trace_id: 01FQWZ4K
decision_sequence:
  - evaluate_policies: matched tier=premium, region=eu-west
  - check_quota: remaining_tokens=1200, req_tokens=800 -> ok
  - selector: variant=v1a (gpu-rtx) preferred
  - capacity_probe: candidate_capacity=0.85 -> below threshold for v1a
  - fallback: choose v1-quant (cpu/quantized) reason=capacity_pressure
  - post_route: applied_prefix_cache=false
````
jon: nice. capacity_pressure -> we should expose the probe score and the rule that triggered fallback (capacity_threshold, cost_override, quota_exhausted). right now Console only shows final model name.
sasha: Agreed. Minimal UX needs: (1) request-level breadcrumb (policy matches -> quota check -> capacity probe -> final route), (2) numeric probe scores, (3) collapseable raw headers, (4) link to account quota snapshot at time of request.
liam: For telemetry, add these metrics: `routing.decision.count{final_variant}`, `routing.fallback.count{reason}`, `routing.probe.score` histogram, and `routing.headers.sampled` gauge of samples/sec. Also tag by region and tier.
ara: We should also surface quick filters in the Console: show all requests where fallback.reason=capacity_pressure AND tier=premium AND region=eu-west. That would let SEs triage without a trace.
jon: UX idea: Decision timeline bar in request detail: left-to-right boxes showing each step with hoverable tooltip containing the raw condition and value that caused the step. color code: green=pass, amber=soft-fallback, red=hard-fallback.
maya: +1. Also need a lightweight playback mode for reproducing routing: spawn a synthetic request with the saved headers and a toggle to force different capacity_probe scores to see where it would have routed.
liam: Playback needs to be safe: sandboxed and rate-limited. add an ACL so only SE/ops can trigger for customer orgs. record the playback as an evaluation run for audits.
ara: On the API side, can we add an optional `X-Redwood-Debug: routing=full` header that signals sampling of full decision trace into the 30d retained debug logs? customers can toggle for their org or we sample at 0.1% by default.
sasha: Love that. Implementational note: traces can be heavy; store condensed decision events + pointers to metric snapshots instead of full payloads. keep a hashed pointer to original request body for repro when allowed.
jon: For rollout UX: when deploying a variant rollout (canary -> 10% traffic), Console should show two views: aggregate routing split by policy (e.g., tier breakdown) and a live trace stream filtered for the new variant so we can see why traffic didn't flow as expected.
maya: Example recent case: premium account with bursty traffic got routed to cheaper variant because «capacity_probe» was evaluated with a 0.6 threshold and current load produced 0.58. If the rollout targeted premium only we missed it because Console aggregate split was across all tiers.
liam: So we need per-policy overlays in rollout dashboard and the ability to restrict sampling to policy-scoped traffic.
ara: small API contract suggestion for the headers: `X-Redwood-Routing: tier=premium; region=eu-west; prefer_variant=v1a; debug=1` and an opt-in `X-Redwood-Routing-Signature` for verified routing inputs to aid audits.
jon: Also add structured enums for fallback reasons in telemetry: capacity_pressure, quota_exhausted, model_degraded, cost_override, region_unavailable, fallback_policy. keeps dashboards clean.
sasha: Frontend ask: show the top 3 reasons for fallback per time window and let users click a reason to see example traces. also surface the median probe_score for candidate variants.
maya: QA: can we sample more heavily for Premium during the initial week of rollout? helps catch these region-specific issues.
infra-bot: deploy.ready - routing-traces-indexer v2 scheduled to roll at 2026-03-22T03:00Z; will add probe_score field and fallback_reason tag.
liam: Cool. infra-bot, can the indexer add backfill for last 72h of high-pri accounts?
infra-bot: deploy.note - backfill job queued for 72h window; will respect data retention and PII scrubbing rules.
ara: next steps: 1) eng-platform to spec telemetry enums + metrics (jon, liam) 2) eng-ux to prototype decision timeline + filters (sasha) 3) runtime to add probe_score + decision trace sampling header (maya) 4) infra to ship indexer + backfill (infra-bot)
jon: I'll sketch a minimal proto JSON for the decision trace shape to use in Console: 
jon: ````
{
  "trace_id": "string",
  "timestamp": "ISO8601",
  "routing_headers": "string",
  "steps": [
    {"step":"policy_match","result":"pass","meta":"tier=premium"},
    {"step":"quota_check","result":"pass","meta":"remaining_tokens=1200"},
    {"step":"capacity_probe","result":"soft_fail","meta":"score=0.58,threshold=0.6"},
    {"step":"fallback","result":"applied","meta":"variant=v1-quant,reason=capacity_pressure"}
  ]
}
````
sasha: Looks good. small change: add `user_visible_reason` and `internal_reason_code` so we can surface friendly messages while keeping stable telemetry codes.
maya: I'll open a brief RFC in eng-platform with the shape and the Console mockups. will ping design and ops.
liam: I'll start adding the metrics to the observability proto and a couple Grafana panels for quick checks.
ara: I'll coordinate the access controls for playback and increase premium sampling window for rollouts.
maya: thanks all — let's sync Friday 09:30 PT for a quick triage after infra backfill completes. :raised_hands:
